title: Blackout Beacon — when the internet goes dark, stay in reach.
description: Messages, people and sites in one app. Over the internet when it is up, over its own network when it is not. Free and open source.
hero.h1: When the internet goes dark, stay in reach.
hero.sub: One app for messages, people and sites. When the internet is up it delivers over the internet; when it is not, over Beacon's own network; when both work, over both. No account and no server, and with no internet at all a single hotspot is enough.
hero.meta: Phones need no install. Scan a QR code from the computer.
hero.mobile.cta: Send this link to a computer
hero.mobile.meta: Beacon runs on a computer. Phones need no install: scan the computer's QR code.
off.h: No tower, no router, no server
off.sub: Beacon has no central server. Everything lives on your own devices, so it keeps working with no infrastructure at all.
off.1.d: Any hotspot or router is enough, even with no internet behind it. No mobile data needed.
off.2.d: No account, no cloud, no phone number. Messages and sites stay on your devices.
off.3.d: Take messages and sites from one place to another on a flash drive.
off.4.t: The app passes hand to hand
off.4.d: Beacon shares its own installer over local Wi-Fi, so new people can join with no internet.
off.note: Off-grid range is Wi-Fi range: a room, a floor, a building. Radio bridges (LoRa, Bluetooth) come later.
reach.sub: Beacon works out which paths are open. It sends over the internet when it can, over its own network when it cannot, and over both when both are up.
reach.0.d: No network at all. A hotspot and USB still work.
reach.1.d: The same Wi-Fi or LAN at home, in a hall or an office. It works when nothing else does.
reach.2.d: People on the same internet provider as you.
reach.3.d: International links are cut, but domestic routes are still up.
reach.4.d: Everything is open. Messages go over the internet and Beacon's network together.
how.1.d: One file. No account and no phone number.
how.2.d: Scan a QR code, text a code, or say three words over a call.
how.3.t: It keeps going, internet or not
how.3.d: Over the internet when it is up, over Beacon's network when it is not. If something is held up, Beacon says where it is.
feat.1.d: Delivered, waiting in a mailbox, or queued: it tells you plainly every time.
feat.2.d: Notes, notices, files. Drop a folder and people open it in a browser.
feat.3.d: Scan the computer's QR code and chat in the browser.
feat.4.d: If you have a public address, help others find each other.
polite.body: Beacon never knocks on strangers' addresses. It only connects to people and lighthouses you were introduced to.
polite.note: Your provider can still see which addresses you connect to. It cannot read your messages.
prep.h: Get ready while the internet works
prep.note: This page will not load during an outage. Beacon can hand its own installer to the next person.
faq.1.q: How does it work without the internet?
faq.1.a: When the internet is up, messages go over it. When it is not, Beacon uses whatever is left: your Wi-Fi or LAN, your provider's own network, your country's domestic routes. If all of that is down, it works on the same Wi-Fi only.
faq.2.a: No. Scan a nearby computer's QR code and it opens in the browser. An Android app comes later.
faq.3.a: No, they are end-to-end encrypted. When a message travels over the internet, the relays in between see only encrypted text. This version has no forward secrecy yet: if your key is stolen, old messages can be read. If you join from a phone, your messages are kept on that computer and the person who runs it can read them.
faq.4.a: No. It is free and open source under the MIT license.
faq.5.q: Why does Windows show a warning?
faq.5.a: New apps can trigger SmartScreen. Verify the publisher and checksum before running a build. Signing does not guarantee a warning-free download; do not turn Windows protection off.
final.h: Install it before you need it.
footer.privacy: Language uses your browser or your saved choice. No analytics, tracking or country lookup. Fonts and scripts are served from this site.

hero.mobile.sub: One app for messages, people and sites. Over the internet when it is up, over Beacon's own network when it is not. With no internet at all, a single hotspot is enough.
faq.6.q: Is it useful while the internet works?
faq.6.a: Yes. It is an everyday app: it uses the internet when it is up, and when the internet drops you change nothing. It carries on over Beacon's network by itself.
